b.x: Theatre that expires in the dark

The internet teaches stacking rice and counting calories. In concrete Brazil what kills the stock is something else: heat, humidity, moths, rancid oil, an opened pack with no new date, food that only exists if there is gas and water. The kit does not cover that. The pantry does — if you read the three clocks.
DON'T
Do not photograph the shelf. Do not buy what the house does not eat on Tuesday. On day D the mouth refuses what it never ate.
Clock 1 — what is written

The pack date is the least urgent and the only one people look at. It helps. It is not enough. First expired, first out (FEFO). FIFO by purchase order alone leaves the new lot in front and the old one rotting behind. ‘Use by’ is not ‘best before’. One is safety. The other is quality. Mixing them throws good food in the bin or puts bad food on the table.
A mixed lot with no tape on the lid is a blind stock. Tape with month/year on the front of the can. Without tape, the house chooses in the dark.
If the family does not eat it on Tuesday, do not buy it for ‘day D’.
Clock 2 — the opened pack

Here the stock dies with nobody watching. Flour, milk powder, oats, coffee, oil, an opened preserve, a biscuit pack ‘to nibble’: the box date died on the day of the cut. Another clock starts — short, damp, with oxygen.
01 Opened: write the date on tape in the same minute.
02 A jar only if it is dry, clean, with a lid that truly shuts. A ‘pretty glass’ jar with damp flour becomes moths.
03 A wet scoop in the rice is an invitation. A hand in the sack too.
04 Opened oil in heat goes rancid months before the date. Rancid is not fuss: it is oxidised fat. Change it.
05 An opened preserve goes to the fridge in clean glass, never in the dented can.
CAUTION
Whoever stores 20 kg and opens one sack a month with no new date does not have 20 kg. They have one living sack and nineteen forgotten ones.
Clock 3 — the house’s climate
American advice of ‘cool and dry’ is a joke in Brazil if the pantry is the service area, above the stove, or a wall that takes the four-o’clock sun.
Humidity enters the paper sack and ‘loose’ rice. Weevils and mould do not ask for collapse. They ask for a wet March.
Heat speeds the rancid of oil, nuts, milk powder, a bar with fat.
Light eats vitamin and colour. It is not aesthetics. It is a nutrient that goes.
The floor is rodent and flood. First shelf above the knee. A flood does not warn the bean sack.
The stove and an external fridge heat the wall. A pantry stuck to the oven ages the oil in silence.
Tuesday test — ten minutes, paper
01 Does this shelf take sun or bath steam?
02 Is there an opened sack with no date?
03 Is the oil away from heat?
04 If gas fails for three days, what on this shelf still becomes a plate?
05 If the water rises to the knee, what is lost?
DO
What fails, goes up, gets sealed, or leaves the stock. Do not argue with the wall. Pocket card: /kits/relogios. No calculator. No brand. No photo.
Food that needs fire and water is half food
Rice, beans and pasta without water and without heat are stone. Advanced stock is not more kilos. It is a possible plate. Three layers in the same house, without announcing it in the window.
01 No stove — a can with an opener, sardine, tuna, a preserve eaten cold, a bar, dried fruit, milk powder if there is cold water, sliced bread on a short turn, rapadura, nuts if the climate allows.
02 Cold water only — the same, plus what hydrates without a boil if the house accepts it.
03 With a burner and one litre — rice, quick pasta, soup, beans already cooked and frozen in portions, not the raw 10 kg sack as the only bet.
CAUTION
Whoever only has the raw sack bet on public service: power, gas, water in the pipe. Water to cook counts in the stock. Dry beans without an extra litre are not food. They are work.
What the stock forgets and the house pays
Fat and salt. Plain rice tires and does not hold whoever works or cares for a child.
Protein the house already accepts. Egg only exists if the fridge is alive. Can and beans exist if there is rotation.
Meds that eat with food. Stock without the blood-pressure pill or the sugar of whoever is diabetic is an indecent shelf. The plan is the doctor’s, not the forum’s.
Baby, elder, whoever does not chew the dry. Internet-average stock ignores real teeth and stomachs.
Trash and hygiene. Food is left over. Illness arrives before hunger if soap and a way to wash the hand are missing.
NOTE
Do not build a 90-day island if the house does not yet turn 14. Fourteen days of Tuesday’s plate beat a year of anonymous cans.
What this field refuses
It does not teach a bunker in the window.
It does not teach a pantry photo.
It does not teach food nobody in the house touches.
It does not teach ‘survival food’ with an operator’s name.
It does not replace medical advice or the local sanitary rule.

It teaches only this: stock is rotation + climate + a possible plate without theatre. Tape on the lid. FEFO in front. Oil away from the stove. An opened sack with a new date. Something you eat if the gas dies. Water that cooks what you stored. If the house does not eat it on Tuesday, it is not stock. It is weight that expires in the dark.
